name: iratebirds - Rate the Appearance of Birds (1-10 Hearts)
description: Method replication: the iratebirds citizen-science task for measuring how attractive people find different bird species. Participants see bird photographs one at a time in random order and answer "Please rate the appearance of this bird!" on a scale of 1 to 10 hearts. After 10 birds they answer the paper's background survey (Table 1: five 1-5 items on identifying common and rare birds, joy in seeing birds, paying attention to birds and time outdoors; three yes/no items on birding and environmental memberships and a nature-based profession; country, birth year and gender), and can then keep rating as many of the remaining birds as they like. The original app showed one of the five best user-rated Macaulay Library photos per species, which cannot be redistributed; this template uses one openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photo for each of 29 well-known species, from House Sparrow and Feral Pigeon to Mandarin Duck, Shoebill and Snowy Owl, each credited under the photo. The published iratebirds score for each species (raw mean and model-corrected) is stored in the page, so new ratings can be compared with the 408,207 original ratings from 6,212 people. Differences from the original study: (1) 29 species with one Wikimedia photo each instead of about 11,000 species with up to five Macaulay Library photos each; (2) English only instead of 20 languages; (3) answers to the background survey are required here, while in the app it was optional; (4) the photos were resized to at most 1200 px.
author: Haukka, Lehikoinen, Mammola, Morris & Santangeli

config.description: Participants rate photographs of bird species, one at a time in random order, on how much they like each bird's appearance (1-10 hearts). After 10 birds they answer the iratebirds background survey (bird identification skills, joy and attention to birds, time outdoors, memberships, profession, country, birth year, gender), then may keep rating. Method replication of Haukka, Lehikoinen, Mammola, Morris & Santangeli (2023), Scientific Data 10: 297; the original Macaulay Library photos cannot be redistributed, so this template uses one openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photo per species (credited in the page). Analysis: mean rating per species; compare with the published iratebirds score for each species (stored in the page).
